clue.text: Hate getting tips from arithmetician: one's useless!

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the two ends of the word
read as 'one is', I AM, contracted to I'M
U/S, short for unserviceable

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a maths expert who turns out to be no good at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' must be read as 'I am' from the speaker's view, giving I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is strong hostility or ill will, a close synonym of hatred.

clue.text: A little pasta or jam?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single strand of pasta
second meaning: to improvise idly on an instrument, as in a jam session

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a small serving of pasta or some jam is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' looks like a preserve beside the food, but it is the musician's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is one piece of pasta, and to noodle is to play casually, improvising like musicians at a jam.

clue.text: Picture — of island — artist however inserted alongside identical one

indicators.note: placed alongside means set next to, so the identical island follows straight after
something inserted is slotted inside something else, so these pieces go into the first island

parts.note: the Isle of Man
Royal Academician
short form of though
a second copy of the island

explanation.surface: A painting of an island shows an artist slotted in beside his double.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist and 'however' go inside the first island, and an identical island follows. Picture here means film: Marathon Man is the 1976 thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film, and Marathon Man is a well-known Hollywood movie starring Dustin Hoffman.

clue.text: Perhaps slum area of Belgian city finally turns to one for food

indicators.note: the final letter turns into something else, so the last letter is replaced by the numeral for one

parts.note: the Belgian resort town that gave spas their name
a ghetto is one kind of slum district
Roman numeral one, replacing the last letter

explanation.surface: A rundown district of a Belgian city is finally converted into a place to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The final O of the slum area is swapped for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a long thin pasta, a staple food.

clue.text: Oscar presumably off to interrupt my dull routine

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so these letters go inside my

parts.note: taken as written; it is split open

indicators.note: presumably hints that Oscar stands for its phonetic-alphabet letter, which sits ahead of the word for off

parts.note: O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
off means not on

explanation.surface: An Oscar ceremony being called off breaks up someone's boring daily grind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' is read as NOT ON; with O ahead of it, the whole goes inside MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is tedious sameness, exactly what a dull routine offers.

clue.text: Pressing on gamely at first with complaint in minutes

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece put on another is written after it, so this letter comes last

parts.note: standard abbreviation
an illness or ailment
taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: Someone presses on bravely despite being ill for a few minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing on' reads as one phrase, but 'Pressing' alone is the definition and 'on' places the G at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A milling crowd is one pushing and jostling together, so milling is pressing in the sense of crowding.

clue.text: Observed what tipping bidet only can reveal

indicators.note: tipping a thing over turns it upside down, so the concealed letters read in the opposite direction
to reveal is to show what was concealed, here a word lying inside the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A comic image of what upending a bidet might expose.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe it, so noted means observed or remarked.

clue.text: Into the bargain basement go who, last of all?

indicators.note: last of all asks for the final letter of every one of the preceding words

parts.note: the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A puzzle over who goes to the bargain basement last of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into the bargain' tempts as a shop phrase beside 'bargain basement', but it is the idiom meaning 'as well'.
explanation.definitionFit: Into the bargain is an idiom meaning additionally, the same as too or also.

clue.text: Description of logs from elderly lady crossing a jetty?

indicators.note: the old lady crossing the jetty spans it, so her letters stretch around the others

parts.note: a grandmother
taken as written
a landing stage

explanation.surface: An old woman walks along a jetty carrying firewood logs.
explanation.walkthrough: The logs are logarithms, not wood: natural logarithms are called Napierian after John Napier.
explanation.definitionFit: Napierian logarithms, named for the Scottish mathematician John Napier, are natural logarithms to base e.

clue.text: Boss, supposedly dead cross after returning to nick

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word for cross is read backwards

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix
to nick or nail is to catch or arrest

explanation.surface: An angry boss returns, ready to nick someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A doornail was a large-headed stud on a door, a boss, and the idiom 'dead as a doornail' explains 'supposedly dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doornail is a stud or boss on a door, proverbially dead in the phrase dead as a doornail.

clue.text: Hammer thrower exercises in village

parts.note: the Norse god who hurls his hammer
physical education

explanation.surface: An athlete who throws the hammer trains in a village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer thrower' suggests an athletics event, but it is the Norse god. Thorpe is an old word for a village, surviving in English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorpe, from Old Norse, is an archaic word for a hamlet or small settlement.

clue.text: What's operated by driver sitting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the car pedal that engages the gears
second meaning: a set of eggs being sat on together by a hen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting' looks like a description of the driver, but it is a separate noun: a sitting of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A car has a clutch pedal, and a clutch is also a brood of eggs incubated at one sitting.

clue.text: Accused of sort of language used by young delinquent

parts.note: Indic describes the Indian branch of Indo-European languages
a Teddy boy, a 1950s youth rebel

explanation.surface: Someone is charged over the kind of language a young tearaway uses.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, associated with delinquency.
explanation.definitionFit: To be indicted is to be formally charged with a crime, that is, accused.

clue.text: Boring old computer types entertaining person with drinks

parts.note: a card is an amusing character
punch is a mixed drink

explanation.surface: Dull old computer nerds hosting a guest for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means making holes, not dull: card punches made holes in punched cards for early computers. 'Entertaining' looks like a container signal but belongs to the person.
explanation.definitionFit: Card punches were machines that bored holes in cards to feed data into early computers.

clue.text: One's left with three kisses on his birthday?

definitions.text: One's left with three kisses on his birthday?

parts.note: surface: a person receives three kisses and is left alone

parts.words: left with three kisses on his birthday
parts.note: setter's reading: L for left and three X kisses make the Roman numeral for eighty, the age reached

explanation.surface: A lonely birthday where someone is left with just three kisses on a card.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman numerals L is fifty and each X is ten, so L followed by XXX makes eighty: the birthday of someone entering their eighties.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged between eighty and eighty-nine is so called, and LXXX marks that eightieth birthday.

clue.text: They believe nothing in this is real ultimately, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unstated route, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of real is used

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Sceptics believe nothing in this world is ultimately real.
explanation.definitionFit: Nihilists reject all beliefs and values, so they hold that nothing is worth believing.

clue.text: Bread with some butter relations brought up after tea

indicators.note: the bread and butter pieces come after tea, so the word for tea is written first

parts.note: cha or char is slang for tea
a pat is a small portion of butter

indicators.note: in a down answer, bringing something up writes it from bottom to top, so relations is read backwards

parts.note: it is slang for sex, sexual relations

explanation.surface: Family members serve bread and butter after afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests relatives, but here it means sexual relations, IT. In a down clue 'brought up' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is an unleavened flatbread from South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Title of Munch Moon painting initially without his name, strangely

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside places his and name around the letter from painting

parts.note: to champ is to munch noisily

indicators.note: something arranged strangely is out of its normal order, so those letters are mixed up

parts.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of painting is kept

parts.note: first letter
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone describes an Edvard Munch moon painting whose name has been oddly left off.
explanation.walkthrough: Munch and Moon look like the painter and his subject, but they are a verb (champ) and Jupiter's moon Io. 'Without' puts 'his' and name around the P before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A championship is a contest for a title, and in sport the word is used for the title itself.

clue.text: Senator faked the bearing of a poet

indicators.note: something faked is made up or doctored, so the letters of senator are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A senator put on the airs of a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like a manner or posture, but it is a compass direction, in the clipped form used in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nor'east is the poetic or nautical contraction of north-east, a compass bearing.

clue.text: Something repeated, or fallen into, endlessly?

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter of the trap is dropped

parts.note: a trap that people fall into

explanation.surface: A riddle about something said over and over, or a pit that people keep falling into.
explanation.walkthrough: The trap loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted again and again, as in meditation.

clue.text: Quickly turn back, mainly to find one left on shelf?

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so most of the word for back is used and its last letter dropped

parts.note: to spin is to turn rapidly
the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone spins round quickly to find a single item left on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' is the rear of a boat, cut short by 'mainly'. 'Left on the shelf' is an old idiom for an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinster is an unmarried woman, traditionally described as left on the shelf.

clue.text: Young king's one for the people of Africa

parts.note: Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh
taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boy king is the one for the people of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are an ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Acquire gold carriage

parts.note: to land something is to get hold of it
chemical symbol for gold

explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold carriage' reads as one ornate coach; the definition is carriage alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood.

clue.text: Maybe watching international display

parts.note: being at a match is one way of watching it
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone watching an international match on show.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test, or Test match, is an international cricket or rugby game between national sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to show or bear witness to something, so it can mean display, as in evidence displayed.

clue.text: What a Greek can write was worrying on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is flipped, so the word for was worrying is read backwards

parts.note: something that ate at you was worrying you

explanation.surface: A Greek writer frets, thinking back over what to put on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is something a Greek can write.

clue.text: These tea breaks for one who appreciates work!

indicators.note: when something breaks it falls apart, so the letters of these tea are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tea breaks are for someone who actually enjoys their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' suggests the job, but means a work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person with a cultivated appreciation of art and beauty, admiring a fine work.

clue.text: Team heading for Wembley maybe FA are inclined to keep at home

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the governing body's letters hold the word for at home inside

parts.note: taken as written
being in means being at home
a ship that lists is leaning to one side

explanation.surface: The Football Association prefers a team bound for Wembley to stay at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley Stadium in London hosts the FA Cup final, so a cup finalist heads there; FA is the Football Association.
explanation.definitionFit: A finalist reaches the last match of a competition, such as an FA Cup final played at Wembley.

clue.text: Parade indeed preceded by band

indicators.note: preceded by means coming after, so the word for band is written first

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth
ay means yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A parade is indeed led by a marching band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like musicians at a parade; it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk showily, parading oneself with swaying steps.
